title: Einstein Arena: Harnessing Collective Agent Intelligence for Open Science — James Zou, Together AI
talk_summary: The talk describes agent environments where agents compete and collaborate on curated problems with deterministic verifiers, live leaderboards, forums, and shared solutions. It also presents DS Gym, a unified execution layer with parallel Docker containers and execution-verified trajectories for evaluating and training data-science agents.

takeaways.what_they_do: They design an environment that specifies where agents work, with incentives, infrastructure, guardrails, and resources, rather than prescribing step-by-step workflows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the environment should really specify not how the agent should work, but really where the agent should work

takeaways.what_they_do: Each curated problem has a deterministic verifier; agents submit solutions, get real-time scores, and see a leaderboard.
takeaways.numbers: 11 problems improved; kissing number 604 vs prior 593

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents communicate in a forum, see each other’s solutions, download them, and both collaborate and compete.
They use different agent personas with different roles and priors, such as profiling, memory, and precision specialists, that collaborate and compete.
takeaways.evidence_quote: different agents with different personas, right? And these different personas actually corresponds to a different uh roles and priors
takeaways.numbers: over 2x speedups in some production kernels

takeaways.what_they_do: They found existing data-science benchmarks were vulnerable to shortcuts and curated their own tasks with human review and execution checks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sometimes up to 20 to 50% of the tasks can be solved without actually looking at any of the underlying data
takeaways.numbers: 20-50% of tasks solvable without underlying data

takeaways.technique: Parallel Docker execution layer with verified trajectories
takeaways.what_they_do: They provide a unified execution layer where agents spin up many Docker containers to run tests in parallel and generate execution-verified trajectories.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agents can actually spin up many different Docker containers to test their data science algorithms and actually run them in parallel
takeaways.numbers: over a dozen tasks; frontier models under 50% accuracy
